# Neoism's pinned Rune input patch

These packages are imported unchanged from `anomalyco/rune` at `e970367bd7d2a51e2e7d58e2978ea32eac7780cb`, except for the touch-policy, native Metal frame-extension and live-text remount changes described below and the reduced workspace manifest with explicit package workspace paths. Upstream's MIT license and package assets/licenses are included. Only Rune and its four local package dependencies are included; unrelated upstream packages and workspace-level examples are not vendored.

Local changes separate touch panning from mouse selection/dragging and cancel read-only selection tracking when a finger starts panning. File-tree rows opt into hold-to-drag; editor text opts into touch scrolling. Ordinary sliders and scrollbars retain their existing touch-drag behavior. Regression tests live in `rune/app/src/touch_tests.rs`.

The macOS host also needs actual touch events. `vendor/winit-compat/winit-0.30.13/MACOS-DIRECT-TOUCH.md` documents the AppKit bridge, which admits direct-screen contacts without intercepting indirect trackpad touches. A mouse-only display driver cannot be distinguished from a real mouse by this layer.

When updating Rune, carry or upstream these patches rather than modifying the Cargo checkout. The app patches these five Git-source packages to local paths; `rune-kit` and its other dependencies retain their original Git pin.

Virtual-only scroll remounts accept live text without rebuilding the view or staying rows. Before the first content-changing live sample, the runtime retains the authored text spec for intrinsic measurement; retained nodes therefore never measure the sampled label, even after a layout-cache miss. Paint layout uses the same uncached live-run path as normal sampling, including when an unchanged source keeps its seen token. Subscription rebuilding and end-of-frame sampling remain unchanged. Focused regressions for stable and updated text, placeholder measurement, glyph geometry/clipping, entering/staying rows and later live wakes run from the repository root with `rune/app/build.sh test --manifest-path ../vendor/rune/Cargo.toml -p rune --test live_remount`. This public-runtime target does not require the omitted upstream shader and font fixtures that currently prevent compiling the vendored unit-test target.

The bundled `.metallib` and `.dxbc` files are upstream GPU shader libraries embedded with `include_bytes!`, not local app executables or stray build outputs. Font files and binary rendering-test fixtures are also required upstream assets. Keep these versioned for reproducible fresh checkouts; root `.gitattributes` identifies the dependency as vendored and the shader/data blobs as binary. Local app builds and packaged releases belong in the already-ignored `target/` and `dist/` directories or external build caches.

`src/native_frame.rs` adds a macOS per-AppKit-view pre-present encoder callback for the native Metal backend. `gpu/metal/surface.rs` carries the view identity and physical/logical scale with each drawable and enables non-framebuffer-only drawables when a hook is installed. Surface destruction removes the hook. `gpu/metal/submit.rs` invokes it after Rune's encoders have closed and before commit/present, then signals a final event value so frame pacing includes the extension. The extension must retain its resources until command-buffer completion: Rune command buffers use unretained references. There is no additional command queue, CPU pixel readback, drawable presentation, private API, or wgpu-hal dependency. The app owns the original shader and small GPU backdrop blit; see `rune/app/native/README.md`. wgpu and other backends do not invoke the callback and retain the ordinary cursor fallback.

`platform/display_link.rs` decides which display-link ticks draw. Upstream skipped a tick that came less than half a refresh period after the last submission, whatever started that frame; a frame started on a tick that took more than half a period (4.2 ms at 120 Hz) therefore always cost the next refresh, halving the rate while the whole period was free. Here a tick is skipped only when the last frame was submitted after that tick's callback ran (it overran into the tick's slot); the half-period spacing is kept for a frame drawn at once on no tick. The callback records when it ran (`Callback::fired`). `RUNE_TRACE_TICKS=1` prints each decision; `RUNE_TRACE_GPU=1` (`gpu/metal/submit.rs`, `frame/present_time.rs`) prints each frame's commit, GPU start/end and presented time. Unit tests for the rule are in the module; they share the vendored unit-test target's missing-fixture limitation.
